argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Dialectical progression with successive refinement and critique
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate—premises are embedded in thought experiments and formal examples rather than enumerated as numbered propositions

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High—the text fairly presents the indexing solution before critiquing it, and engages with Plantinga's sophisticated version rather than attacking a strawman
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High—each section directly advances the central thesis about the insufficiency of property-indexing
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate—the text relies on contested metaphysical intuitions (e.g., haecceitism, mereological essentialism) without fully defending them

explicit_definitions_given: PI: if x and y are identical, then every property of x is a property of y
PII: if x and y share all their properties, then x and y are identical
Essential properties: those an object has in all possible worlds where it exists (Plantinga's definition)
World-indexed properties: properties of the form being-F-in-w

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: The text raises objections against the indexing solution (triviality, arbitrariness) and then examines Plantinga's response, showing it fails to answer the epistemological objection
objections_raised: If all properties are indexed, identity becomes trivially analytic
If only some properties are indexed, we need a criterion for distinguishing essential from accidental properties—which the indexing mechanism cannot provide
The indexing solution is neutral between competing metaphysical theories (mereological essentialism, haecceitism, bundle theory) and cannot decide between them

epistemic_stance_and_voice.certainty_language_frequency: Low—the text uses hedged language ('seems to', 'appears to', 'threatens to') when discussing contested claims

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Thought experiments and formal logical analysis

philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Critical of formal solutions that fail to address substantive metaphysical questions

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that property-indexing is a necessary formal device for preserving Leibniz's Laws but is insufficient as a metaphysical solution. The indexing mechanism cannot distinguish essential from accidental properties, and Plantinga's attempt to ground it in haecceitism fails to answer the epistemological objection. The paradoxes of identity are thus not resolved but relocated to the unresolved question of essence.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Negative—the proposed solution (property-indexing) is shown to be inadequate
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: High—the text uses 'threatens to', 'seems to', 'appears to' when discussing the failure of Plantinga's account
